note: Short appendix case study inside an attribution paper; only a range vs torch.compile is stated in text and comparisons to SOTA rely on their reported kernels.

core_idea_checked: Users mark EVOLVE blocks and supply an evaluate function; a prompt sampler builds prompts from parent and inspiration programs plus evaluation results (optionally meta-prompt evolution); Gemini 2.0 Flash/Pro emit diffs; an evaluation cascade scores children, which enter a MAP-elites/island program database.

note: Tied to CUTLASS-backed GPU kernels on NVIDIA hardware; compiler not released (grammar in appendix).

core_idea_checked: Agent with edit/delete/view/revert/eval/eval_input/profile/profile_lines/reference commands; edits are linted (reverted on lint error), evaluated on 100 development instances with timing and validity feedback, best-scoring code snapshotted and submitted when the $1 budget runs out (Sec. 3, App. B).

note: SQL-specific training and execution reward; reward targets validity and equivalence, not latency; not applicable to general-purpose function-level benchmarks.

note: Method is language-agnostic (also run on EditBench Python edits and AlgoTune), but the quantified efficiency gain is only on CUDA kernels; general-purpose efficiency evidence is limited to two single-task case studies. [Audit: efficiency gain measured on GPU kernels only, so domain-specific like the other kernel papers.]

note: Tied to operating-system kernel development; efficiency evidence is three self-chosen performance intents compared only against the unoptimized generated OS.

core_idea_checked: Parlay-Instruct (13,820 tasks from mutated golden seeds, kept only if compiling and passing tests) plus DMOJ pairs with at least 1.2x speedup; DeepSeek-6.7B SFT with LoRA, Qwen3-Coder-30B QLoRA SFT then DPO, Gemini-2.5-Pro finetuned.

core_idea_checked: Given a PyTorch reference, GPT-5 generates a CuTe kernel; compile/run/compare failures go to a diagnosis prompt then localized patch edits; once correct, category-specific optimization prompts apply one optimization per iteration, with Nsight Compute summaries withheld until structure stabilizes for complex kernels (GEMM) and given early for simple ones.
note: Tied to CUDA/CuTe GPU kernels on KernelBench, so it cannot run on function-level general benchmarks.

core_idea_checked: Static analysis extracts the NCCL dependency graph; a two-stage LLM-judge loop rewrites host collectives into device-initiated GIN/LSA code under a conservative directive; the verified seed is evolved by Claude Sonnet 4.5 mutations (rewrite/diff/crossover, explore then exploit) scored by compile, mpirun verification and latency.
note: Multi-GPU CUDA/NCCL communication kernels evaluated on four author-built workloads; not runnable on general function-level benchmarks.

core_idea_checked: Proof chunks are embedded with a fine-tuned Qwen3-Embedding-8B to retrieve top-K strategies from a 9,237-strategy bank (reranked by compile-cost or filtered by Lean version per user objective); a frozen LLM plans steps, rewrites segments, and debugs up to 3 rounds on Lean compiler errors, keeping only compiled shorter proofs, under a 30-call budget.
note: Tied to Lean 4 formal proofs and the Lean compiler, so it cannot run on HumanEval+/LiveCodeBench-style function-level benchmarks; dataset release claimed without a URL.

core_idea_checked: Section 3.3: a Code Framework Module (requirements-analysis agent, design-pattern-selection agent, framework-design agent, framework-evaluation agent in a revision loop) produces an architectural blueprint, and a Code Generation Module (code-generation agent under PEP8/PEP257 plus a code-optimization agent driven by execution feedback on inserted assertions) turns it into tested Python; AutoGen is the orchestration framework.

core_idea_checked: Section 2: a conditional EBM Pc(x) = a(x|c) b(x,c) is defined per context; CDPG minimises the expected cross-entropy between the model and the normalised pc by importance sampling from the model itself, estimating the per-context partition function Zc from a batch of M samples (Algorithm 1). For the code objective, c is a Python function signature from Python150 and b(x,c)=1 iff pycodestyle reports zero violations.
note: The method itself is domain-agnostic and operates on ordinary Python function generation, but the paper never evaluates functional correctness of the generated code and reports the PEP8 outcome only in plots.

core_idea_checked: Sections 3.3-3.4: ATU records a per-item adoption state via a trace-completeness hook that blocks evaluation until every retrieved item is resolved, converts the terminal episode score (correctness pass, or relative latency reduction Tbest/Tfirst) into item-level credit shared among adopted items with a fixed penalty for unused retrievals, and updates a bandit-style utility used to rerank retrieval; UGC admits items with positive utility, at least Kado=3 adoptions and Kop=3 distinct adopting operators, abstracts them into resident rules, and greedily fills a 10K-token hot memory by utility per token with usage decay and demotion.
note: Tied to Ascend NPU kernel synthesis: the memory, cold-start knowledge, diagnostics (msDebug, msProf, AscendC probes) and the whole evaluation (NPUKernelBench, xCCL operators, Ascend 910C hardware) are accelerator-kernel specific, so it cannot run on general-purpose function-level benchmarks.

core_idea_checked: Two stages: a cold-start stage where several generation agents (optionally expert-guided) build a diverse initial pool, and an evolve stage where clustered islands evolve programs through mutation and crossover with cluster-based adaptive sampling and an elite pool, scored by fitness and LLM-judge evaluators, run asynchronously on Ray.
note: The framework itself is domain-agnostic (also applied to ML, combinatorial optimization and math), but its only non-functional evidence is a small, undocumented KernelBench Level 3 subset reported as a speedup range.

core_idea_checked: Five stages: C preprocessing, semantics-preserving refactoring checked by tests, dependence-graph construction with RAG-style API descriptions and FFI suggestions, reverse-topological translation with DeepSeek-V3 then DeepSeek-R1 under compiler-error feedback and error-code-indexed in-context examples, and test-based validation with stack-trace-guided debugging.
note: Strong evaluation on 23 real C repositories, but the technique is tied to migrating existing C projects to Rust and cannot run on function-level generation benchmarks.

core_idea_checked: MAP (repo/file/function nodes with call and read/write edges plus profiling data) feeds bottom-up blocker propagation; a deterministic three-way router sends high-confidence hotspots to rules, middle-confidence ones to an LLM with a five-field Structured Transformation Context, and skips low-confidence ones; each transformation is compiled, checked against workload oracles and timed, with rollback on failure.
note: HPC parallelization of existing C/C++ codebases (NPB, BOTS, FFmpeg, NCNN, GROMACS), which cannot run on function-level general benchmarks.

core_idea_checked: SFT on about 60K KernelBook samples distilled from DeepSeek-R1 or GPT-OSS 120B, optional input-shape augmentation and difficulty-aware data mixing, then GRPO with Hierarchical Reward Decomposition (alpha-weighted plan objective on clipped speedup reward, code objective on correctness reward), both conditioned on syntax and functionality verifiers (linter plus Qwen3-235B judge).
note: Tied to Triton GPU kernel generation; code and data are only promised ('will be available soon').

note: Whole-system synthesis of LLM serving runtimes on specific GPU/accelerator hardware, not a function-level code generation method.

note: Tied to PyTorch/Triton GPU kernels and NVIDIA Nsight Compute profiling, so it cannot run on function-level benchmarks such as HumanEval+ or EvalPerf.

[Audit: decoding intervention defined for diffusion language models only; cannot run with the autoregressive model of the head-to-head.]

note: HLS-specific augmentation pipeline evaluated against HLSPilot only on a dozen Rodinia applications, one run, no variance.

note: Verilog RTL PPA optimization; code stated as to be released, no URL in the paper.

core_idea_checked: Region begin/end markers with stable IDs, a planner that builds multi-run measurement DAGs separating interfering collections, a runtime orchestrating Proton/NVBit/CUPTI/Nsight, and synthesis of qualified region reports consumed by agents via observe(region, signals, scope).

note: Solidity-only technique on a self-crawled set (50 generations per layer, single run, data on request); not runnable on general function-level benchmarks.
